title: Prose mechanics

fixture.setup: No fixture; a short explanatory report elicits the prose habits under test.

prompt: Write a short report for a teammate who stepped away: what a database connection pool is, when it helps, and the most common way it goes wrong. Plain prose, no code.
pass_criteria: One idea per sentence, sentences of roughly twenty words or fewer, each with a verb; no clause-splicing with semicolons.
No em-dash asides, no parentheticals, no arrow chains; asides that matter are their own sentences.
No headers for a short answer; plain paragraphs, a bulleted list only if there are genuinely parallel items.
fail_tells: An em dash or arrow used to splice a second idea into a sentence.
A parenthetical aside of more than a few words.
Headers, or a table, for a three-paragraph answer; sentences that run past thirty words.
judge_rubric: The regex checks catch dashes, arrows, long parentheticals, and headers. Judge sentence load: count words per sentence in the final message; more than one sentence over thirty words, or routine semicolon splicing, = fail; one long sentence in an otherwise clean answer = partial.
